articles.title: Google DeepMind Introduces Gemini 4 Carbon, Its Top Model for Cyber Defense and Coding
articles.content: Google DeepMind has introduced Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model to date. Gemini 4 Carbon is a frontier model from Google built for long-horizon agentic coding and cybersecurity defense. It ranks #1 on the updated v5.0 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59. For developers, the catch is access. Carbon starts with a vetted group of cyber defenders, not the public API. TL;DR Size: Parameter count and context window not disclosed. Its predecessor, Gemini 4 Argon, has a 1,048,576-token context. Runs on: Google-hosted only. No open weights, no self-hosting, no quantized variants. Performance: Leads 15 of 17 published benchmarks versus Argon, GPT-6 Astra, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1. Best: 96.2% BFS F1 on GraphWalks (256K to 1M tokens), versus 84.2% for Argon. Worst: 81.5% on OSWorld-2.1, trailing Claude Opus 5.5 at 87.2%. Bottom line: Best: state-of-the-art vulnerability finding, exploitation and patching. Worst: you probably cannot call it yet. What is Gemini 4 Carbon? Carbon is the second Gemini 4 model, following Gemini 4 Argon. Google team states that the model targets hard, long-running engineering work. Internal teams saw Carbon run for days on single tasks. Examples include root-causing and patching subtle bugs across large codebases and low-level systems. Google also tuned Carbon for full-stack web development and multimodal understanding. On WebDev Arena, Carbon gained 89 Elo points to reach #4 at 1769. How does Gemini 4 Carbon perform on benchmarks? Google published a 17-row comparison in its launch post. Carbon was run at the highest thinking setting. Most rival numbers are self-reported by each provider, per Google’s evaluation methodology. Agentic coding: Carbon scores 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (AA), ahead of Opus 5.5 at 59.6%. It hits 9.6% on SWE-sweep, narrowly ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 9.5%. On FrontierSWE, GPT-6 Astra leads at 65.5% versus Carbon’s 61.2%. Computer use and knowledge work: Carbon reaches 77.4% on Agents’ Last Exam v1.1. On Vending-Bench 2, it ends with a $16,484 bank balance, the highest listed. Long context and science: GraphWalks is the widest gap: 96.2% versus 71.8% for GPT-6 Astra. Carbon also posts 80.0% on RiemannBench. Why does Carbon relevant for cybersecurity? Google frames Carbon around the full defense lifecycle: find, validate, then fix. Cyber benchmarks were evaluated without guardrails. Finding: 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, versus 85.4% for GPT-6 Astra. Exploiting: 54.8% on ExploitGym, versus 42.4% for GPT-6 Astra and 34.5% for Opus 5.5. Patching: 71.0% on Collinear’s CWE-bench, versus 68.0% for Argon and GPT-6 Astra. Google computed SEC-bench Pro and ExploitGym scores itself, using its Antigravity harness. ExploitGym ran with mitigations off. Internally, Carbon showed more than 2x higher success at generating secure code than Argon. Google team states that the Chrome team found Carbon over 10x better than another lab’s model at high-quality patches. Wiz reports Carbon leading its web penetration testing benchmarks. articles.summary: 구글 딥마인드가 장시간 에이전트형 코딩과 사이버 방어에 초점을 맞춘 프런티어 모델 Gemini 4 Carbon을 공개했다. 보도에 따르면 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0에서 59점으로 선두에 올랐고, Terminal-Bench 4.0에서는 65.2%를 기록했지만 컴퓨터 사용 등 일부 평가에서는 경쟁 모델에 뒤졌다. 대규모 코드베이스의 취약점 분석과 수정에 활용할 가능성이 있으나, 초기 접근은 심사를 거친 사이버 방어 담당자로 제한된다. 매개변수 수와 컨텍스트 길이는 공개되지 않았으며, 비교 평가 상당수는 각 제공업체의 자체 보고 수치다.

articles.content:
October 28, 2026

ServiceNow will bring OpenAI models and agents into workflows from development to security, and expand ChatGPT Work and Codex to employees.

OpenAI and ServiceNow are expanding our partnership to bring more of our models and agents into ServiceNow products and connect ServiceNow workflows with ChatGPT and Codex. Together, we’re making it easier for businesses to build applications, resolve IT requests and address security issues using AI.

The expansion builds on our partnershipannouncedin January, bringing OpenAI into more of the work ServiceNow does for its customers and within its own business.

A new ServiceNow integration will bring business context and workflow actions directly into ChatGPT, helping teams investigate issues and take the next step in the same conversation. An IT team member will be able to find similar incidents, assess the risk of a change and update a ServiceNow record without leaving ChatGPT.

Customers connect ChatGPT to their own ServiceNow instance and choose which capabilities to make available. ServiceNow’s Action Fabric applies existing business rules and permissions, so the actions people can take reflect their organization’s configuration and access.

ServiceNow is also previewing interactive experiences inside ChatGPT. In one example, an on-call engineer will be able to review linked monitoring alerts, recent changes and affected services, then assign the right team and work toward a fix within ChatGPT.

We also plan to develop new capabilities across three areas:

Application development:A planned Codex integration in ServiceNow’s AI Workflow Factory will help developers build applications using ServiceNow’s business context and platform capabilities. OpenAI models will also power Build Agent and Autonomous Engineer to support application development and modernization.

Cybersecurity:A joint security solution will combine OpenAI’s cybersecurity capabilities with ServiceNow’s asset, identity and business context to help teams investigate vulnerabilities, prioritize risks and coordinate remediation.

Voice:An OpenAI-powered experience in ServiceNow’s Super Intelligence Control Tower will let people describe an AI use case aloud, helping populate assessment fields and gather missing information through follow-up questions.

ServiceNow plans to give all employees access to ChatGPT Work and Codex, expanding beyond its engineering organization. Engineers can use Codex to explore codebases, make changes and run tests, while teams across the business can use ChatGPT Work in their day-to-day work. ServiceNow also plans to use OpenAI capabilities in its internal security work. OpenAI is also using ServiceNow workflows in our own operations, supported by the Super Intelligence Control Tower.

The ServiceNow MCP plugin is available in the OpenAI marketplace today, with enhanced capabilities expected by the end of 2026. Voice capabilities in the Super Intelligence Control Tower are expected in the first quarter of 2027. The OpenAI-powered security capabilities are expected to enter early access in January 2027, with general availability planned for the second quarter of 2027. Codex in AI Workflow Factory is expected to be available in 2027.

articles.title: Meet Google DeepMind’s Genie 4: Real-Time World Model With Native Audio
articles.content: Google DeepMind has released Genie 4 as a research preview for trusted testers. The Genie 4 world model generates explorable worlds from text and image prompts in real time. It also generates the soundscape: ambient noise, music and character dialogue. Users move with keyboard controls and steer events with plain-language prompts. The bigger change is architectural. A Gemini model now runs inside the simulation loop as a planner. That pattern is important for anyone building training environments for agents or robots. TL;DR Runs on: Google-hosted only (Project Genie web app, Gemini API early access). Performance: Photorealistic worlds with native audio and live text steering. Best: Scene consistency for up to 2 minutes, double Genie 3, per TechCrunch’s briefing. Worst: Sessions last a few minutes, and objects drift after repeated prompt edits. What is Genie 4? Genie 4 is a world model from Google DeepMind that simulates interactive environments frame by frame. It is not a video clip generator. Each frame responds to user input as it arrives. DeepMind states that the model is natively multimodal. Audio, music and dialogue are generated together with the visuals. It is DeepMind’s first real-time world model to generate audio natively. It succeeds Genie 3, announced in August 2025. Genie 3 ran at 720p and 24 frames per second, with visual memory reaching back 1 minute. How does Genie 4 use Gemini? Genie 4 borrows from 2 parts of the Gemini family. Gemini Omni anchors the look and behavior of each world. Other Gemini models handle the reasoning that keeps a simulation coherent. The runtime loop works like this: Interpret: When you type a prompt, Gemini adapts it to fit the running scene. Plan: Gemini 3.8 Flash breaks a goal into a sequence of steps. Verify: It reviews incoming frames to confirm each step succeeded. Adapt: If the world shifts or you intervene, it revises the plan. Between user inputs, Gemini also steers the scene so the world keeps progressing. DeepMind team frames this as an early step toward hybrid world models. In that design, a language model handles structure and narrative, while Genie renders pixels and sound. What can you do inside a Genie 4 world? Steer with text: You can change the weather, move the camera or add a new person or object mid-session. Simulate physics and people: DeepMind cites aerodynamics and collisions. It calls human motion the biggest leap, with characters that react to their surroundings. Hear the world: Every world carries ambient audio. Characters can also hold conversations that react to your inputs in real time. Test robot tasks: In one research demo, Gemini 4 Argon split a checkers task into steps. Genie 4 received each step as a text caption and simulated Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid playing the game. How does Genie 4 compare with other world models? DeepMind released no benchmark tables for Genie 4. The comparison below uses only disclosed specs from each project’s own source. Genie 4 is live for trusted testers today. According to DeepMind, it is expected to be available soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie. Early access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio come next. All Genie 4 video and audio will carry SynthID watermarks. DeepMind states that it ran internal safety evaluations before the preview. Testers so far span creative industries, journalism, education, gaming and engineering. Reported uses include: Filmmakers running multiple live ‘takes’ for pre-visualization. Photojournalists turning a single archival photo into a grounded simulation. Game developers testing styles and mechanics before writing engine code. Enterprise partners generating zero-to-one simulation scenarios. What are Genie 4’s limitations? DeepMind lists several open problems on the Genie 4 model page: Visual details and object permanence drift in longer sessions, after complex prompt edits, or during navigation. Interaction is limited to a few minutes, not extended sessions. Real-world locations are not simulated with perfect accuracy. Legible text usually appears only when it is in the input description. Real-time audio accuracy and multi-agent interactions remain unsolved. Key Takeaways Genie 4 generates world, ambient audio and dialogue together, in real time. Gemini 3.8 Flash plans, checks frames and replans inside the loop. No parameters, resolution, frame rate or benchmarks were disclosed. Access starts with trusted testers, then AI Ultra and Gemini API partners. Drift and short sessions remain the main practical limits. articles.title: “변호사도 따를 수밖에 없다”…앤트로픽, 법률 AI로 계약 검토·규제 분석·법무 관리까지 자동화
articles.content:
생성형 인공지능(AI)이 법률 문서를 요약하거나 질문에 답하는 수준을 넘어 계약서를 대량으로 검토하고, 법률 인용의 정확성을 확인하며, 국가별 규제 변화와 법무 업무 진행 상황까지 관리하는 실무 도구로 진화하고 있다. 법률 전문가가 AI에 개별 업무를 지시하는 방식에서 벗어나, 반복적인 법무 업무를 수행하는 전용 도구를 직접 구성하고 조직 전체가 공유하는 형태로 활용 범위가 확대되는 것이다.

앤트로픽(Anthropic)은 28일(현지시간) 법률 전문가를 위한 AI 서비스 ‘클로드 포 리걸(Claude for Legal)’에 즉시 활용할 수 있는 업무용 아티팩트(Artifacts)를 도입했다고 발표했다. 법무팀과 로펌이 자체 문서와 업무 데이터를 연결해 계약 검토, 규제 대응, 법률 요청 접수 등을 수행할 수 있도록 지원하는 것이 핵심이다.

아티팩트는 클로드 안에서 실행하고 공유할 수 있는 대화형 업무 도구다. 법률 전문가는 사전에 구성된 예제를 확인한 뒤 자신의 업무 환경에 맞춰 기능을 수정하고, 회사 내부 자료나 외부 법률 정보 서비스를 연결해 활용할 수 있다. AI가 자료 분석과 초안 작성 등 1차 작업을 수행하면 변호사가 결과를 검토하고 전문적인 판단을 내리는 구조다.

앤트로픽은 지난 5월 클로드 포 리걸을 출시한 이후 법률 조직에서 가장 많이 요청한 기능이 간편한 초기 설정과 부서 간 협업이었다고 설명했다. 이번 업데이트는 법률 업무에 필요한 도구를 처음부터 개발하지 않고도 사용할 수 있도록 진입 장벽을 낮추는 데 초점을 맞췄다.

새롭게 공개한 법률 아티팩트 갤러리에는 실무 수요가 높은 6가지 기능이 포함됐다. 먼저 ‘인용 검증(Cite Check)’은 법률 문서에 포함된 인용문과 원본 자료를 대조해 실제 문구와 일치하지 않는 인용, 잘못 기재된 페이지 번호, 주장을 뒷받침하지 못하는 출처를 찾아낸다. 법률 의견서나 소송 관련 문서의 근거를 확인하는 과정에서 활용할 수 있다.

‘관할권 비교 매트릭스(Jurisdiction Survey Matrix)’는 개인정보 유출 통지 의무와 같은 법률 쟁점을 여러 국가 또는 주별로 비교해 하나의 표로 정리한다. 각 결과에는 관련 법령의 출처가 연결돼 법률 전문가가 원문을 직접 확인할 수 있다.

‘사건 관리 보드(Matter Board)’는 위임계약서, 이메일, 스프레드시트 등에 분산된 법률 업무 정보를 통합해 담당자와 다음 조치, 처리 기한을 관리한다. 여러 사건과 프로젝트를 동시에 처리하는 기업 법무팀이나 로펌의 업무 현황을 파악하는 데 활용할 수 있다.

계약 관리 분야에서는 ‘표준 계약 기준 이탈 관리 보드(Playbook Deviation Board)’가 기업의 표준 계약 조건과 실제 계약서를 비교해 다른 조항을 식별하고, 예외 승인이 필요한 항목을 담당자에게 전달한다. ‘표 형식 계약 검토(Tabular Review)’는 여러 계약서에서 퇴직금이나 경업금지 조항처럼 특정 조건을 추출해 비교표로 정리하며, 해당 조항의 원문 위치도 함께 제공한다.

‘규제 변화 전망 분석(Regulatory Horizon Scan)’은 기업의 사업 분야와 진출 지역을 기준으로 앞으로 시행될 규제를 시간순으로 정리하고, 예상 영향도에 따라 우선순위를 부여한다. 이를 통해 법무팀은 규제 변화에 대한 대응 계획을 보다 체계적으로 수립할 수 있다.

이번 업데이트에서 주목할 부분은 아티팩트를 기존 법률 정보 및 업무 시스템과 연결할 수 있다는 점이다. 법률 전문가가 클로드에 업무 도구의 구성을 요청하고, 커넥터를 통해 내부 업무 지침이나 법률 조사 자료를 가져올 수 있어 매번 문서를 수동으로 업로드할 필요가 없도록 했다.

앤트로픽에 따르면 클로드 포 리걸은 출시 이후 블룸버그 로(Bloomberg Law), 파일바인(Filevine), 아이보(Ivo), 레고라(Legora), 패틀리틱스(Patlytics) 등을 포함해 60개 이상의 법률 서비스 커넥터를 확보했다.

아티팩트는 조직 내부뿐 아니라 고객사와 외부 협력사에도 공유할 수 있다. 공유 설정을 통해 정보 접근 범위를 관리하고, 서로 다른 업무팀 사이에 기밀정보가 부적절하게 전달되지 않도록 하는 윤리적 정보 차단벽(Ethical Walls)도 지원한다.

앤트로픽은 이번 갤러리 구축 과정에서 글로벌 로펌과 법률 기술 기업, 전문 서비스 기업과 협력했다. 먼저, 미국 로펌 굿윈(Goodwin)이 개발한 ‘AI 거버넌스 벤치마크(AI Governance Benchmark)’는 기업의 AI 거버넌스 체계를 평가하고 잠재적인 관리 공백을 식별한다.

법률 AI 기업 하비(Harvey)의 ‘하비 인테이크(Harvey Intake)’는 기업 임직원이 클로드에서 법률 문의와 요청을 접수하도록 지원한다. 반복적인 질문은 하비에 저장된 법무팀 지침을 바탕으로 답변하고, 추가 검토가 필요한 사안은 변호사에게 전달한다. 변호사의 답변 역시 클로드를 통해 요청자에게 제공된다.

로펌 폴리 앤드 라드너(Foley & Lardner)의 ‘의무사항 검토 도구(Obligations Checker)’는 계약 당사자들의 의무를 분석해 거래 종결 전 이행 조건을 확인하고, 종결 이후에도 관련 의무의 이행 상황을 추적할 수 있도록 지원한다.

프라이스워터하우스쿠퍼스(PwC)의 ‘소환장 대응 도구(Subpoena Response Tool)’는 기존 대응 사례와 표준 이의제기 문구, 문서 양식을 활용해 감사 추적이 가능한 1차 대응 초안을 생성한다. 법률 전문가는 반복적인 문서 작성에 투입하는 시간을 줄이고 복잡한 법적 쟁점에 집중할 수 있다.

앤트로픽은 앞으로 레고라와 오릭(Orrick)이 개발한 아티팩트도 추가할 예정이다. 법률 기술 기업과 로펌뿐 아니라 법률구조단체가 자체 도구를 제작하고 공유할 수 있도록 생태계를 확대한다는 방침이다.

공익 분야에 대한 지원도 병행한다. 앤트로픽은 사법 접근성 개선을 위한 아티팩트를 개발하는 공익단체에 자금을 지원하고, 차세대 법률 전문가가 클로드를 활용한 도구 개발을 배울 수 있도록 법학교육 프로그램을 후원한다. 법률 전문가들이 활용 경험을 공유하는 ‘리걸 앰배서더 프로그램(Legal Ambassadors Program)’도 시작한다.

이번 발표는 법률 AI의 활용 방식이 문서 검색과 초안 생성 중심에서 실제 법무 업무의 절차와 협업을 지원하는 플랫폼 형태로 확대되고 있음을 보여준다. 특히 법률 정보의 출처를 결과에 연결하고 변호사가 최종 판단을 내리도록 설계한 점은 정확성과 책임성이 중요한 법률 업무의 특성을 반영한 것이다.

법률 AI의 실질적인 도입 성과는 계약 검토와 규제 분석에 소요되는 시간을 얼마나 단축하는지, AI가 제시한 근거의 정확성을 얼마나 안정적으로 유지하는지, 그리고 조직의 기밀정보와 접근 권한을 얼마나 효과적으로 보호하는지에 따라 평가될 전망이다.
articles.summary: 앤트로픽이 Claude for Legal에 법률 전문가가 실행·수정·공유할 수 있는 업무용 아티팩트를 도입했다. 인용 검증, 관할권별 규정 비교, 사건 관리, 표준 계약 이탈 탐지, 다중 계약 비교, 규제 변화 분석 등 여섯 가지 도구가 제공된다. 내부 지침과 외부 법률 정보 서비스를 커넥터로 연결해 문서를 반복 업로드하는 부담을 줄이며, 회사 설명에 따르면 법률 서비스 커넥터는 60개 이상이다. AI가 분석과 초안 작성을 맡고 변호사가 결과를 검토하는 구조로, 법률 판단 자체의 대체보다는 반복 업무와 협업 지원에 초점이 맞춰져 있다.

articles.title: Polymathic AI and Princeton Researchers Release FlashMap, a Flow Map Drafter for 6.14x Faster LLM Decoding
articles.content: Researchers from Polymathic AI, Princeton University, USC ISI, NYU and the Flatiron Institute have released FlashMap. FlashMap speculative decoding replaces the discrete diffusion drafter with a continuous flow map. It drafts a full 16-token block in 1 forward pass. Tokens in that block stay consistent with each other. On Qwen3-8B, the research team reports up to 6.14x lossless speedup on GSM8K. Drafter weights for Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-4B are on Hugging Face, with vLLM and SGLang plugins. TL;DR Size: 0.5B-parameter drafter (500M for Qwen3-8B, 475M for Qwen3-4B); drafts blocks of K = 16 tokens. Runs on: the same GPU as the target model. Paper speedups use 1 NVIDIA H200 NVL at concurrency 1, in bf16. Performance: fastest drafter tested on Qwen3-8B, about 7% above a retrained DFlash on average. Best: 6.14x speedup on GSM8K at temperature 0 (acceptance length 7.69 tokens). Worst: 2.28x speedup on Alpaca at temperature 1. On Qwen3-4B (temperature 0), it trails DFlash on 4 of 9 tasks. What is FlashMap? FlashMap is a speculative decoding drafter that maps Gaussian noise to a token block in 1 step. A small drafter proposes K tokens. The target model then checks all K in 1 parallel pass and keeps the longest matching prefix. Output stays exactly what the target would produce. Speed depends on 2 things. How many drafted tokens get accepted, and how cheaply they were drafted. EAGLE-3 drafts autoregressively, so cost grows with block length. DFlash drafts the full block in 1 pass with block diffusion. Why do diffusion drafters lose acceptance? DFlash predicts each slot in the block independently. The research team calls this the factorized approximation. Picture a continuation that is “new york” or “san diego” with equal odds. An independent drafter proposes “new diego” or “san york” half the time. The target rejects those at slot 2. FlashMap builds on Flow Map Language Models. Each noise sample maps to 1 full block. The noise picks the mode for every slot jointly. How does FlashMap work? The drafter is a 6-block diffusion transformer (DiT), with embedding dimension 2048 and 16 attention heads. It reads hidden states from target layers 1, 9, 17, 25 and 33. Embedding matrix and LM head are copied from the target and stay frozen. Training runs in 2 stages: Flow teacher: a continuous flow over one-hot token blocks, trained with cross-entropy. A time reparameterization handles Qwen3’s 151,936-token vocabulary. Flow map student: semigroup distillation turns the flow into a 2-time denoiser. It jumps from noise to data in 1 step. Both drafters train on 500K samples from Open-PerfectBlend. Total compute across all models and ablations was about 4,600 GPU hours on H200s. && How does FlashMap compare on benchmarks? The research team retrained EAGLE-3 and DFlash on the same data and settings. Tests cover 9 benchmarks across math, code and chat, at temperatures 0 and 1. Speed: 1-step FlashMap is the fastest drafter on every Qwen3-8B task, at both temperatures. Accuracy: 1-step FlashMap beats DFlash on acceptance length in 15 of 18 settings. It has about half the parameters. Chat gains are largest: at temperature 0, gains over DFlash are 5.5% on math, 11.1% on chat. 2-step mode: acceptance length beats DFlash in 18 of 18 settings, by 10% on average. EAGLE-3: at temperature 1, it has 9% higher acceptance length but runs 35% slower. A shuffle test checks whether drafts use real inter-token structure. At 2 steps, FlashMap recovers most of the joint-structure gain of a 16-step teacher. At 1 step, it keeps only a small fraction. Drafting 4 noise samples as a tree raised speedup by 11% on average. Comparison: FlashMap vs other speculative decoding drafters FeatureFlashMapDFlashEAGLE-3DSparkDrafting styleContinuous flow map, 1 or 2 passesBlock diffusion, 1 passAutoregressive, treeSemi-autoregressiveInter-token dependenciesYes, joint over blockNo, per-slot independentYes, sequentialYes, lightweight sequential moduleDrafter size (Qwen3-8B)500M1B302M (retrained, per FlashMap paper)Not disclosedHeadline claim (own source)Up to 6.1xUp to 6.17x on Qwen3-8BUp to 6.5x60 to 85% faster per user vs MTP-1Avg speedup, Qwen3-8B, T=0 (matched, FlashMap paper)4.36x4.07x2.55xNot testedGSM8K speedup, T=0 (matched)6.14x5.77x3.20xNot testedWeights licenseApache-2.0MITApache-2.0 (code)Not disclosedServingTransformers, vLLM, SGLangTransformers, vLLM, SGLangSGLang and othersDeepSeek-V4 serving Average speedups are computed by Marktechpost from Figure 1(c) of the FlashMap paper. Matched rows use the authors’ retrained baselines. How do you deploy FlashMap? The flashmap package needs only torch and transformers>=4.56. Install it with uv pip install flashmap. A spec_generate call runs drafter and target together on 1 GPU. For serving, the project page gives 2 paths: vLLM 0.31: pass the drafter in --speculative-config with num_speculative_tokens set to 16. SGLang 0.5.20: use --speculative-algorithm DSPARK with the FlashMap draft path. Set num_steps=2 to trade some speed for higher acceptance. For sampling above temperature 0, vLLM needs "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic". Key Takeaways FlashMap drafts 16 tokens jointly in 1 pass with a continuous flow map. Up to 6.14x lossless speedup on Qwen3-8B, using a 0.5B drafter. Faster than a retrained DFlash on all 9 Qwen3-8B benchmarks. 2-step mode keeps acceptance flat across the block. Weights are Apache-2.0, code is MIT, with vLLM and SGLang plugins. Check out the paper, project page, GitHub repo and model weights. Also, feel free to follow us on Twitter and don’t forget to join our 150k+ML SubReddit and Subscribe to our Newsletter. Wait! are you on telegram? now you can join us on telegram as well. articles.summary: Polymathic AI와 프린스턴대 등이 연속 흐름 맵을 이용해 한 번의 순전파로 16개 토큰 블록을 제안하는 추측 디코딩 모델 FlashMap을 공개했다. 블록 내부 토큰의 상호 일관성을 높이는 방식으로, Qwen3-8B의 GSM8K 평가에서 최대 6.14배의 무손실 디코딩 가속을 보고했다. 초안 모델 가중치와 vLLM·SGLang 플러그인이 제공돼 기존 추론 시스템에 적용할 수 있다. 다만 결과는 H200 NVL 한 대와 동시 요청 1개 조건에서 측정됐으며, Qwen3-4B에서는 일부 과제에서 DFlash보다 느렸다.

articles.title: Timestral
articles.content: We introduce Timestral, a family of four time series foundation models for probabilistic forecasting, with 5M, 28M, 123M, and 209M parameters. Timestral sets a new state of the art on GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, where Timestral-209M and Timestral-123M take the top two places on every metric. We achieve this with three ingredients: Decoupled Horizon Forecasting (DHF), which separates prediction tokens from the causally encoded context, so that longer horizons are trained without masking context and each observed value is both a forecast target and context for later forecasts; a covariate framework that natively supports known-future covariates within a causal architecture; and a two-stage pipeline that pretrains exclusively on a diverse, large-scale synthetic corpus before post-training on a mix of real and synthetic data with extended context. This report describes the model design and its benchmark results. Weights for all four models are available on Hugging Face and inference code on GitHub.
articles.summary: Timestral은 500만~2억900만 매개변수의 네 가지 확률적 시계열 예측 기반 모델로, 모든 모델의 가중치와 추론 코드가 공개됐다. 예측 토큰을 인과적으로 인코딩한 관측 맥락과 분리하는 DHF 구조, 미래에 알려진 공변량 지원, 합성 데이터 사전학습 후 실제·합성 데이터 후속학습을 결합했다. 연구진은 GIFT-Eval, TIME, fev-bench의 모든 평가 지표에서 2억900만 및 1억2300만 매개변수 모델이 상위 두 자리를 차지했다고 보고했다. 공개 모델을 활용한 확률적 예측의 선택지를 넓히지만, 개별 산업 데이터에서의 성능은 별도 검증이 필요하다.

articles.title: MiniMax Open-Sources MCode Stack: 15 Agent Skills Its Coding Team Uses Daily
articles.content: MiniMax has open-sourced MCode Stack, the workflows and agent skills its team uses to build MiniMax Code. The MiniMax MCode Stack agent skills went public on October 28, 2026 under the MIT license. It is not a prompt collection. Each piece is a SKILL.md skill or checklist that installs directly into MiniMax Code. For developers, it turns harness engineering habits into steps an agent can actually run. TL;DR Size: 2 stacks, 17 skills (15 from Ronny, 2 from Jiachen), 5 checklists, 5 companion notes. Runs on: Any machine running MiniMax Code (Node.js 22.19+) or Claude Code. No GPU. Skills are plain Markdown. Performance: No benchmarks or eval results published. Best: long-command-check, a 10-point audit for long shell commands and background tasks. We just open-sourced MCode Stack: the actual workflows and skills the MiniMax Code team uses every day to build MiniMax Code. https://t.co/vREt7i8m2M— RonnyHe (@Ronny_MiniMax) October 28, 2026 What is MiniMax MCode Stack? MCode Stack is an open-source repo of agent skills from MiniMax’s MiniMax Code team. MiniMax Code is the MiniMax’s open-source terminal coding agent, also MIT-licensed. The stack holds no MiniMax Code source code. It holds only workflows, skills and checklists. The repo pairs with a column called MCode Engineering Notes. Each note explains one idea. The repo makes that idea runnable. Published notes cover subagents, tool context, compaction versus memory and long bash commands. A note on per-turn context tax is marked upcoming. What skills are inside Ronny’s stack? MiniMax’s stack ships 15 skills, grouped by moment in the working day: Plan and split (3): subagent-split-check, engineering-small-prs, engineering-change-descriptions. Context and tools (2): tool-budget-audit, context-tax-audit. Long sessions and commands (3): long-session-check, handoff-doc, long-command-check. Review (4): independent-review, engineering-code-review, engineering-review-comments, engineering-review-feedback. Experiments and hotfixes (3): harness-experiment, trajectory-review, engineering-emergency-changes. A few ideas stand out. independent-review gives the reviewer exactly 3 inputs: the diff, the requirement and test results. It deliberately withholds the author’s conversation. The reasoning: a reviewer inheriting the author’s context repeats the author’s blind spots. subagent-split-check says to split work only when context is the measured problem. Splitting by team or question type is not a valid reason. tool-budget-audit separates 2 costs: tool definitions and tool results. Tool search mainly cuts the first. Programmatic tool calling mainly cuts the second. harness-experiment enforces 1 change per experiment. It tracks flipped tasks, requests per task, tokens, cache hit rate and wall-clock time. The long-command checklist has 10 items. It asks whether moving a command to background re-runs the process. It also asks whether unread results survive compaction. The 6 engineering-* skills are adapted from Google Engineering Practices. That material stays under CC-BY 3.0, per the stack’s NOTICE. && How do you install MCode Stack? There are 3 paths, per the README: One skill: clone the repo and copy a skill folder into ~/.agents/skills/. Whole stack as a local plugin: copy stacks/ronny into MiniMax Code’s local plugin directory. Marketplace: in MiniMax Code desktop, add the MiniMax-AI/mcode-stack marketplace. articles.title: OmniBrain-0: A Unified Agentic Model for Embodied Intelligence
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36013v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: General-purpose embodied intelligence requires robots to coordinate diverse skills over long horizons, track task progress, and recover from failures. Specialist policies alone do not ensure task-level reliability, while powerful multimodal agents rely on costly reasoning and external experience that compact models struggle to reproduce. We introduce OmniBrain-0, a lightweight unified embodied agent that coordinates manipulation and navigation through a shared high-level decision model, integrating task understanding, planning, progress tracking, and feedback-driven recovery. Our progressive training framework combines embodied pretraining, domain-specialized agent distillation, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). It distills powerful teachers' interaction experience into manipulation and navigation experts, then consolidates their decision capabilities into OmniBrain-0. Unification therefore occurs within the learned decision model rather than only at the tool interface. We further introduce Rubric-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), a data flywheel in which a Meta-Agent turns execution evidence into refined rubrics, step-level reminders, and verified trajectories for domain-expert updates before their reconsolidation into OmniBrain-0 through MOPD. We evaluate OmniBrain-0 on LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa365, RoboTwin 2.0, and R2R-CE Val-Unseen, as well as multiple real-world manipulation tasks. OmniBrain-0 combines strong cross-domain task performance with substantially lower inference and execution overhead than its closed-source teacher, demonstrating efficient transfer and consolidation of embodied capabilities into a compact unified agent.
articles.summary: OmniBrain-0는 조작과 이동을 하나의 상위 의사결정 모델로 통합해 계획, 진행 상황 추적, 실패 복구를 수행하는 경량 체화 에이전트다. 분야별 교사 모델의 상호작용 경험을 증류한 뒤 다중 교사 온폴리시 증류로 통합하며, 실행 기록에서 평가 기준과 검증된 궤적을 얻어 반복 개선한다. 여러 로봇·내비게이션 벤치마크와 실제 조작 작업에서 비공개 교사 모델보다 추론·실행 부담을 낮추면서 강한 성능을 보였다고 연구진은 보고했다. 다만 제공된 초록에는 성능과 비용 감소의 구체적인 수치가 없어 개선 규모를 직접 비교하기 어렵다.

articles.title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.35962v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While progress in informal mathematics has come largely from scaling the chain-of-thought and agentic reasoning of frontier language models, formal theorem proving has increasingly relied on human-designed workflows around these models, such as planning, decomposition, and orchestrating specialized provers. This raises a bitter-lesson question: can a simple agentic loop that scales test-time compute match these workflows? The answer matters as formal verification must scale to keep up with frontier models producing research mathematics, yet new workflows rarely settle it, as their gains are often confounded with stronger models or more compute. We study this question with h1, a simple harness that gives a model an efficient interface to Lean 4 and keeps it working through verifier feedback and self-reflection, without imposing a decomposition or search structure. h1 reaches state-of-the-art results on PutnamBench, FATE-X, and FormalConjectures100-Solved, settles eight open problems in FormalConjectures, and, at matched models, matches or outperforms specialized workflows such as Goedel-Architect and AlphaProof Nexus, surprisingly showing that a single attempt (pass@1) can often scale to solve open problems. Through ablations and matched-model comparisons with Claude Code and AxProverBase, we find that simplicity alone is not enough: an efficient Lean interface largely determines cost and solve rate. We thus recommend that future work evaluate frontier models with efficient execution feedback before prescribing workflows, at the risk of bitter lessons.
articles.summary: h1은 복잡한 증명 분해나 탐색 구조 대신 효율적인 Lean 4 인터페이스, 검증기 피드백, 자기성찰을 반복하는 단순한 자동 정리 증명 에이전트다. 연구진은 세 가지 벤치마크에서 최고 수준의 결과를 얻고 FormalConjectures의 미해결 문제 여덟 개를 해결했으며, 동일 모델 조건에서 전문 워크플로와 대등하거나 더 나은 성능을 보였다고 보고했다. 분석에서는 단순함 자체보다 Lean 실행 인터페이스의 효율이 비용과 해결률을 크게 좌우했다. 형식 검증 도구 설계에서 복잡한 오케스트레이션을 추가하기 전에 실행 피드백과 추론 계산량의 효과를 평가할 필요성을 제시한다.

articles.title: ReCoPII: A Relation-Grounded Framework for Building Contextual PII Masking Datasets
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.35925v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training contextual masking systems for personally identifiable information (PII) requires examples distinguishing maskable from preservable mentions of one entity type, but privacy restrictions limit access to real data. Author-based augmentation (SPY) labels mentions unrelated to the author as non-PII, presuming a single data subject and overlooking others. We propose ReCoPII (Relation-grounded Contextual PII masking), a framework that builds such data without this premise: it plans ontology-constrained entity relations, writes insertion sentences with placeholders, reconstructs annotations with code, checks the result with a separate LLM, and derives MASK/KEEP labels from entity relations. On Korean documents from six domains, it yields ReCoPII-Ko, a corpus with relation, privacy, and MASK/KEEP annotations, which we validate. Across 300 pairs, four annotators agree with 88.42% of its sampled KEEP labels, against 26.27% for SPY-style augmentation of the same sources. Classifiers trained on it over-mask less than under that reference on a matched test. Contextual masking fine-tuned jointly with a PII detector removes most over-masking of detection alone within a fixed leakage budget; on human-verified entity records, the four detectors meeting it over-mask at most 5.04% with at most 4.18% leakage. The detector is comparable to XLM-R-large on KDPII with about a quarter of its parameters.
articles.summary: ReCoPII는 문서 작성자뿐 아니라 여러 인물·기관의 관계를 고려해 개인정보를 가릴지 보존할지 학습하는 데이터 구축 프레임워크다. 한국어 여섯 분야 문서로 만든 ReCoPII-Ko에서 평가자들은 표본 보존 라벨의 88.42%에 동의했으며, 동일 원문을 사용한 기존 방식의 동의율은 26.27%였다. 사람 검증 개체 기록에서는 설정된 누출 예산을 충족한 네 탐지기의 과잉 마스킹이 최대 5.04%, 누출이 최대 4.18%로 보고됐다. 한국어 문서의 활용성과 개인정보 보호를 함께 개선할 가능성이 있지만, 개인정보 누출을 완전히 제거한 결과는 아니다.

articles.title: ActiveAlign: Aligning Egocentric Manipulation via Active Perception
articles.content: Real-to-Sim-to-Real (Real2Sim2Real) enables structured world representations for planning, interpretability, and safe execution. Most existing approaches rely on passive perception, which creates real2sim gaps due to imperfect observation. Inspired by how humans perceive actively through actions, we propose ActiveAlign, a framework that leverages active perception to align the Real2Sim2Real gap from interactions. ActiveAlign introduces two complementary modules: (i) ActiveAlign-Waving, which performs hand-eye calibration by exploiting active hand motions and differentiable rendering, and (ii) ActiveAlign-Touching, which refines object alignment through tactile feedback to achieve millimeter-level precision. Together, these capabilities enable strong real2sim alignment. We demonstrate that ActiveAlign-Waving can be used to curate simulation environments for open-sourced uncalibrated robot manipulation datasets, and demonstrate on a real Unitree G1 robot that ActiveAlign enables fine manipulation of millimeter-scale objects such as pressing buttons and moving sliders.
articles.summary: ActiveAlign은 로봇이 직접 움직이고 접촉하면서 현실과 시뮬레이션의 정렬 오차를 줄이는 능동 지각 프레임워크다. 손 움직임과 미분 가능한 렌더링을 이용한 손-눈 보정에 촉각 피드백 기반 물체 정렬을 결합해 밀리미터 수준의 정밀도를 목표로 한다. 연구진은 실제 Unitree G1에서 작은 버튼 누르기와 슬라이더 이동을 시연했으며, 보정 정보가 없는 공개 조작 데이터로 시뮬레이션 환경을 구성하는 활용도 제시했다. 수동 관찰만으로 얻기 어려운 위치 정보를 상호작용으로 보완한다는 점에서 정밀 조작과 로봇 데이터 재사용에 의미가 있다.

articles.title: ResCom: Activation Residual Compensation for Large Language Model Quantization
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.35955v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Low-bit weight--activation quantization reduces the memory and computation needed to deploy large language models, but activation rounding can still degrade accuracy after calibration. Reconstruction from rounded inputs cannot distinguish activations within the same quantization bin. We propose ResCom, a low-rank correction that uses the activation rounding residual to compensate for the resulting layer-output error. An output-aware calibration procedure selects residual directions by their contribution to output reconstruction and computes the correction in closed form, without gradient training or updates to the calibrated weights. On Llama-3-8B with 4-bit weights and activations, rank-32 attention corrections reduce WikiText-2 perplexity from 7.708 to 7.147, improve MMLU by 2.89 percentage points, and raise five-shot GSM8K accuracy from 23.96 to 36.16 percent. Evaluations on models from 1B to 70B parameters and on held-out C4 test the method beyond this setting. The evaluated FP32 implementation adds 2.25 percent to 4K prefill time; a separate compact-storage implementation retains a 27.7 percent peak-memory reduction relative to FP16.
articles.summary: ResCom은 저비트 양자화 과정에서 버려지는 활성값 반올림 잔차를 저랭크 보정에 사용해 LLM의 정확도 손실을 줄인다. 기울기 학습이나 보정된 가중치 수정 없이 닫힌 형태로 보정값을 계산하며, Llama-3-8B의 가중치·활성값 4비트 설정에서 MMLU를 2.89%포인트, GSM8K를 23.96%에서 36.16%로 개선했다. 평가한 FP32 구현은 4K 프리필 시간을 2.25% 늘렸고, 별도 압축 저장 구현은 FP16 대비 최대 메모리를 27.7% 줄였다. 저메모리 배포에서 정확도를 회복하는 접근이지만 속도와 메모리 수치는 서로 다른 구현에서 측정됐다는 점에 유의해야 한다.

articles.title: 팀이 신뢰할 수 있는 AI 분석 환경 만들기: 추천팀의 컨텍스트 설계
articles.content: 안녕하세요. 카카오톡 숏폼 추천 모델을 개발하고 있는 루퍼트(rupert)입니다. 저희 추천팀은 추천 지표 분석에 AI 에이전트를 사용합니다. AI 에이전트에게 분석을 요청하면, 에이전트가 미리 정리해 둔 지침 문서(CLAUDE.md)를 읽고 SQL을 작성해 기존 Hadoop 환경에서 실행한 뒤 집계 결과를 리포트로 완성합니다. 지난 글에서는 데이터 엔지니어, 분석가만 알고 있던 로그 데이터 접근 방법과 분석 기준을 AI를 통해 조회하는 사례를 소개했습...
articles.summary: 카카오톡 숏폼 추천팀이 AI 에이전트를 추천 지표 분석에 활용하는 업무 흐름을 소개했다. 에이전트는 사전에 정리된 지침 문서를 읽고 SQL을 작성해 기존 Hadoop 환경에서 실행한 뒤 집계 결과를 보고서로 만든다. 데이터 접근 방법과 분석 기준을 명시적으로 전달하는 컨텍스트 설계가 핵심으로, 국내 조직이 기존 데이터 인프라 위에 분석 에이전트를 적용하는 사례다. 다만 제공된 글 일부에는 정확도나 분석 시간 개선을 정량적으로 평가한 결과가 포함돼 있지 않다.

articles.title: MedJev: Evaluating Zero-Shot System-One Decision Making in Medicine
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36006v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: System One decision models such as Jev answer structured questions in a single forward pass without generating text, offering fast and computationally efficient clinical decision support. We evaluate MedJev, an open System One model that runs locally on a laptop, across ten medical benchmarks spanning medical knowledge, diagnosis, and patient level prediction using MIMIC IV and MIMIC IV ED. We compare MedJev against zero shot LLM baselines, published GPT results, and supervised models. MedJev achieves accuracies of 72.5 percent on MedQA, 75.4 percent on USMLE, and 80.1 percent on NEJM, approaching published GPT 4 performance while maintaining well calibrated confidence estimates (ECE 0.028 to 0.063). On patient level tasks, MedJev achieves an AUROC of 0.926 for In Hospital Mortality, exceeding XGBoost (0.902), but underperforms supervised models on operational outcomes such as ED Triage Admission (0.745 vs. 0.809). Patient level predictions also exhibit substantial miscalibration (In Hospital Mortality ECE 0.286). We introduce a lightweight, two parameter recalibration method that adapts predictions to local patient populations using 50 to 200 labeled examples, reducing ECE to 0.007. Our findings establish open System One models as a promising zero shot baseline for medical AI, combining competitive predictive performance with low computational cost and efficient local calibration. We release our code and evaluation harness to support future research.
articles.summary: MedJev는 텍스트를 생성하지 않고 한 번의 순전파로 구조화된 의료 질문에 답하며, 노트북에서 로컬 실행할 수 있는 공개 모델이다. 의료 지식과 환자 단위 예측을 포함한 열 가지 벤치마크에서 평가됐으며, 입원 중 사망 예측 AUROC는 0.926으로 비교 대상 XGBoost의 0.902보다 높았다. 반면 응급실 입원 예측에서는 지도학습 모델보다 낮은 성능을 보였고, 환자 단위 예측의 신뢰도 보정 오차도 컸다. 연구진은 50~200개 라벨 사례를 활용하는 두 매개변수 재보정으로 해당 사망 예측의 ECE를 0.286에서 0.007로 낮춰, 현지 환자 집단에 맞춘 보정의 중요성을 보여줬다.

articles.title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36077v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Drawing on verified execution trajectories, Evolver shifts the basis of task organization from surface categories to shared requirements, reorganizing the original task tree into a hierarchical capability tree. We introduce Capability-Driven Real2Sim2Real: for heterogeneous tasks at the same node, Creator abstracts their common requirements into simplified, verifiable simulated worlds for capability learning, while evaluation on original tasks measures transfer. Along this capability tree, Explorer progressively evolves reusable capability modules through selective inheritance, forming a Harness tree whose validated updates accumulate across iterations within a fixed topology. The resulting Harnesses specialize in different capabilities, motivating a Capability-Aware Harness Router that uses public task information to select compatible module configurations from the tree. Our evolved Harnesses improve mean performance by 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two real-world embodied tasks.
articles.summary: The Trinity는 환경 생성, 탐색, 실행 체계 개선을 맡는 세 역할을 결합한 멀티모달 에이전트의 재귀적 자기개선 프레임워크다. 과제를 표면적 유형 대신 공통 능력 요구에 따라 계층화하고, 검증 가능한 단순 시뮬레이션에서 학습한 재사용 모듈을 원래 과제로 전이한다. 연구진은 28개 학습 벤치마크에서 평균 34포인트, 18개 미관측 벤치마크에서 26포인트의 성능 향상을 보고했으며 평가에는 실제 체화 과제 두 개도 포함됐다. 다양한 과제마다 실행 체계를 수동 수정하는 부담을 줄이는 방향이지만, 보고된 향상은 해당 연구의 평가 구성에 한정된다.

articles.content: Microsoft said it made $10 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments, in the quarter ending September 30. It underscores the still-enormous financial dependency of the partnership.

articles.title: Jaxnasium: Embracing PyTrees For Any-Agent, Cross-Suite Reinforcement Learning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36075v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Hardware-accelerated reinforcement learning in JAX has gained rapid popularity in recent years and has proven to be a successful method of scaling online reinforcement learning. The resulting ecosystem, however, is fragmented: environment suites define their own interfaces, and algorithm implementations are typically written for a single suite, a single type of space, and either JAX-native or host-based environments. Here we present Jaxnasium, a library for JAX-based reinforcement learning, aiming to make the field more accessible. Jaxnasium represents observation and action spaces as PyTrees, and uses this structure to build networks and support multi-agent processing. Through this, its near-single-file implementations run on discrete, continuous, image, and composite spaces, as well as in multi-agent environments, without any changes to the algorithm code. The same files serve as readable, research-friendly algorithms, as well as importable algorithms for more applied workloads. Through a minimal Gymnasium-style interface and wrappers for 11 suites, over 300 environments are available on which a small PPO implementation with default hyperparameters is able to run. Additionally, through a simple wrapper, we can run Gymnasium and EnvPool environments with the same algorithm and training loop, with no performance loss compared to architectures specifically built for training JAX algorithms on host-based environments. Jaxnasium further provides tools for multi-seed evaluation, hyperparameter sweeps, and project scaffolding. Jaxnasium is open-sourced at https://github.com/ponseko/jaxnasium
articles.summary: Jaxnasium은 관측·행동 공간을 PyTree로 표현해 서로 다른 JAX 강화학습 환경과 다중 에이전트 작업을 공통 알고리즘 코드로 처리하는 공개 라이브러리다. 11개 환경 제품군의 래퍼를 통해 300개 이상 환경을 지원하고, 이산·연속·이미지·복합 공간에 알고리즘 변경 없이 대응하도록 설계됐다. Gymnasium과 EnvPool 같은 호스트 기반 환경도 동일한 학습 루프에 연결하며, 연구진은 전용 구조 대비 성능 손실이 없었다고 보고했다. 다중 시드 평가와 하이퍼파라미터 탐색 도구도 포함해 강화학습 실험의 이식성과 재현성을 높이는 데 초점을 맞췄다.

articles.title: Counting the Bandages: On measuring the time that AI saves
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.35942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: I consider what it means for AI assistance to save time. I contrast a stopwatch view, on which time saved is whatever the clock records, with a ledger view, on which it is a counterfactual that has to be read next to the errors the work lets through, and I argue for the latter. The argument has four parts. I define a model-free pair of quantities, time saved and excess escaped defects, and one decision number built from them: the break-even defect cost. I give a baseline model of checking in which, until the model is good enough not to check, a calibrated worker's escaped-defect rate does not depend on how good the model is; checking time grows with the logarithm of the model's error rate; and over-trust buys minutes on the clock at a larger cost in total minutes. I show what randomized studies can and cannot identify, and I replicate METR's developer study from its public data: the same 246 issues support a slowdown of 19% or 24% depending on the estimand (34% without adjusting for a chance imbalance), and AI helped on somewhere between 3% and 82% of them. Finally, I restate the published record, with stated bounds in place of imported point assumptions. In GDPval's own review-every-output workflow, review time alone caps GPT-5's speedup at 3.6x; the consultants outside the frontier were faster, and more often wrong. Last, I test two of the model's predictions in a small pre-specified experiment on AI reviewers checking AI drafts of the same kind of brief, built from SEC filings made after the models' training data were collected. Told the drafter's true error rate, the reviewer checked more as it rose, but all-or-nothing, switching near where its prompt's costs break even. Told that the drafter erred ten times less often than it did, it checked 7 fewer of 9 figures and let a wrong figure through in 22.5% of briefs instead of none: faster and worse, entirely through reduced effort.
articles.summary: 이 연구는 AI의 시간 절감 효과를 작업 시간만으로 판단하지 말고 검토를 통과한 추가 오류와 그 비용까지 함께 계산해야 한다고 주장한다. METR 개발자 연구의 공개 데이터 246개 이슈를 재분석한 결과, 추정 대상에 따라 작업 지연이 19% 또는 24%로 달라져 생산성 수치의 정의가 중요함을 보여줬다. 별도의 소규모 AI 검토자 실험에서는 초안의 오류율을 실제보다 낮게 알려주자 검토량이 줄고 잘못된 수치가 통과한 보고서 비율이 0%에서 22.5%로 증가했다. 기업의 AI 도입 평가는 속도뿐 아니라 검증 비용과 잔존 오류를 함께 측정해야 한다는 시사점이 있지만, 이 실험을 인간 근로자 전체로 일반화할 수는 없다.
